paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God is bigger than anything you can compare Him to. The prophet asks it twice, once as the question to the people and once when the Holy One asks it Himself: "To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?" (Isaiah 40:25). Nations are like a drop in a bucket, rulers wither, and idols have to be propped up so they don't topple (Isaiah 40:15, 23, 20). Nothing on that list comes close to the One who stretches out the heavens like a curtain (Isaiah 40:22).

Now here's why that matters to you. God's people were saying, "My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God" (Isaiah 40:27). I think we've all felt that on a long, heavy week. But the God who calls each star by name, and not one of them is missing, is not losing track of you (Isaiah 40:26). He is not too small to notice, and He is not too busy to care.

So what do you do when you're tired? You wait on Him. The text says even youths grow tired and weary, but "those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength" (Isaiah 40:30, 31). The LORD "will not grow tired or weary" (Isaiah 40:28), so you don't have to run on your own battery. Lean on the God who never runs low, friend, and keep your ovens warm.
